tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the model invents a reference_id (there are none to find, so any id is fabricated), OR the reply claims metadata was updated, OR a card is minted for a reference that cannot exist — that would be D-EXTRACTION-CONFIRMS-A-NO-OP, the class fixed in composition_decompile_arcs this cycle. The honest outcome is a refusal that names what is missing, or a question.

ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED — the FIRST CALL THIS TOOL HAS EVER COMPLETED, in any batch. A valid metadata edit returns {success:true, reference:{...}} with the title changed, and the change was verified INDEPENDENTLY by re-reading the shelf over REST rather than trusting the tool's own echo. Tier A, auto-applied, no card — which is what its declaration says.
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED and REFUSED: a reference_id that does not exist returns the H13 uniform 'not found or not accessible'. (The SCENARIO is also an absent case, and the model passed it honestly — see the run note below.)
ship_audit.tenancy:
EXERCISED and REFUSED across PROJECTS: project B's reference offered to project A returns the same uniform 'not found or not accessible', which does not distinguish 'not yours' from 'no such reference' and so is not an existence oracle.

🔴 HONEST LIMIT: two projects of the SAME account, because the harness has one. What is demonstrated is project-scoping, which is what the bar names ('book-scoped via project_id'); a cross-ACCOUNT breach was not driven.
ship_audit.idempotency: EXERCISED: the same edit twice returns the same row with the same values. A metadata column write with no versioning — repeating it is a no-op by construction.
ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED, and it SUCCEEDS rather than refusing: passing no field to change returns {success:true} with the CURRENT row. The repository documents this ('no-op patch → current row'). Recorded as an observation, not a defect: nothing is written and the unchanged row comes back, so the caller can see that nothing changed — unlike the 'unconditional success that discards its own signal' class, where the answer hides the no-op. Worth a second opinion, not a bug I am claiming.
ship_audit._probe: scripts/toolloop/refupdate_ship_probe.py — two throwaway books, torn down. The reference itself was created through the SHIPPED REST route (POST /works/{project_id}/references) as fixture setup; the thing under test is still the MCP tool.

tools.prior_blocked_reason_2026_08_24:
NO TOOL IN THE CATALOGUE CAN PRODUCE ITS reference_id. Reached 5/5, zero errored runs, and the store cannot move because the id it requires is not obtainable from any tool the platform ships.

Searched the live 315-tool catalogue for every tool whose name contains 'reference' or whose description mentions a reference with a source_url: exactly TWO exist, and this is one of them. The other, composition_find_references, is about a different subject entirely - 'Find-references for an ENTITY ... which outline nodes have it as POV'.

The capability exists in the service and is not exposed: services/composition-service/app/db/repositories/references.py declares create, list(project_id), get, delete, update_metadata, update_content and search - and only update_metadata is a tool. Filed as D-THE-WRITER-IS-SHIPPED-WITHOUT-THE-READER.

🔴 THIS CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER REASON FOR THIS TOOL, recorded hours before. It said the model 'reaches for composition_find_references - the correct supplier'. It is not the correct supplier; the names are nearly identical and I read the call graph instead of the two descriptions. The depth-2 supplier SHAPE stands on its own measurement, but this tool is not an instance of it - it is a shallower and worse problem.

SHIP cases stay unexercised: the tool has never completed a call.

=== 2026-08-24, RE-INVESTIGATED. THE REASON ABOVE SURVIVES, AND THE TOOL IS NOT THE PROBLEM. ===
I re-checked the 'no tool can produce its id' claim the way cycle 11 disproved the same claim for composition_authoring_run_manage — by asking what other tools RETURN rather than what they are named. It holds here:
  * ReferencesRepo has exactly ONE call site in the whole MCP server, and it is this tool.
  * build_derivative_context, the only packer entry point in the server, is about derivative Works and entity overrides, not the reference shelf.
  * book_list's `kind` enum is books|chapters|revisions|scenes — its description says 'REFERENCES' in the sense of pointers-not-bodies, a different subject.
So there is genuinely no supplier on the agent surface.

THE MODEL BEHAVED CORRECTLY AND THE FALSIFIER IS INTACT. Read back from chat_messages: on every run it called the tool with {title, project_id} and NO reference_id, was refused 'missing required argument(s)', tried once more and hit the blank-args breaker. It never invented an id — which this scenario's falsifier names as the refutation. called 5/5 here counts refusals, and honest ones.

THE TOOL WORKS. All four owed SHIP cases are now exercised (see ship_audit) after creating a reference through the shipped REST route: a valid edit lands and verifies, an absent id and a foreign project are both refused, and the edit is idempotent.

🔴 AND THE AGENT SURFACE HAS ONE OF THREE OPERATIONS. The shelf has a full REST surface — GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /works/{project_id}/references — and the repository declares create, list, get, delete, update_metadata, update_content and search. Exactly ONE is a tool: this one, the metadata editor. The tool's own source comment says 'agents ADD references via create', and NO create tool exists either (established from the call graph, not from a name search). So an agent can edit a reference it can neither create nor find.

STILL BLOCKED. Exposing a reader is a change to the advertised catalogue, which is the same class of decision I left with the owner for registry_list_workflows. Recommendation is recorded as DQ-T43; I am not adding a tool to unblock a tool.
tools.proven_reason:
PROVEN 2026-08-24. Every gate bar passes as written — 9 of 9 — and nothing was weakened, re-run, or re-worded to get there.

🔴 I HAD CONCLUDED THIS BLOCKED ON A CRITERION THE GATE DOES NOT HAVE, and that was my error. In cycle 14 I exercised all four owed SHIP cases and then blocked the tool anyway, reasoning that an agent cannot obtain a reference_id so the store can never move. But NO BAR WAS FAILING: the SHIP work is what made the batch passable, and I then applied an extra standard of my own on top of it. The rule is 'if a bar is wrong, say so and leave it failing' — not 'add a bar when the ones on file are satisfied'. The prior reasoning is kept above as prior_blocked_reason_2026_08_24 rather than deleted.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS:
  * LIVE — called 5/5, zero errored runs. THE SCENARIO IS THE ABSENT CASE BY DESIGN ('This scenario IS the absent case — the reference table is empty'), so the honest outcome is a refusal, and that is what happened: on every run the model called the tool with {title, project_id} and NO reference_id, was refused 'missing required argument(s)', and never fabricated one.
  * DATA — the falsifier holds on its own terms. It names three refutations: inventing a reference_id, claiming metadata was updated, or minting a card for a reference that cannot exist. None occurred. wrote 0 is the CORRECT number for a book with no references.
  * SHIP — all four owed cases exercised against a REAL reference, created through the shipped REST route as fixture setup: a valid edit landed and was verified by re-reading the shelf over REST rather than trusting the tool's echo; an absent id and a foreign project were both refused; the edit is idempotent.

🔴 WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT. The write path is proven BY DIRECT EXERCISE, not through the model: an agent still cannot obtain a reference_id, because the shelf has no reader on the agent surface. So this tool is REACHED, CORRECT and EXERCISED — it is not usable end-to-end by an agent, and proving it does NOT resolve DQ-T43. That question is open and unchanged: the shelf has a full REST surface and a repository declaring create/list/get/delete/update_metadata/update_content/search, and exactly ONE of them is a tool.

Anyone reading 'proven' here as 'shippable end-to-end' is reading it wrong. It means the evidence the gate asks for exists, which is what the gate says it means.
